**James Timothy DuBois** (born May 4, 1948) is an American accountant, songwriter, and recording industry executive based in Nashville. He has headed both Arista Records and Universal South Records,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-unisouthlaunch-1) and as a songwriter, he has written five No.1 country hits, including "Love in the First Degree" which was a world-wide hit recorded by the group Alabama.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-2)

DuBois started playing guitar in bands as a youth. He received three academic scholarships to Oklahoma State University (OSU) to study accounting, earned two advanced degrees, and worked as a senior financial analyst for the Texas Federal Reserve Bank.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-3) He also worked for Arthur Andersen.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-Okla_HOF-4) While pursuing his PhD, DuBois became interested in country music and began writing songs. This eventually led him to move to Nashville to pursue music. Writing successful songs led him to become a record producer, creating over 20 No. 1 and top five singles and more than a dozen gold, platinum, and double-platinum country albums. He founded the musical group Restless Heart in 1984, and Clive Davis hired him in 1989 to establish a Nashville office of Arista Records.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-5) He discovered and signed country artists Alan Jackson, Brooks & Dunn, The Tractors, Brad Paisley, Blackhawk, Pam Tillis and Diamond Rio.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-osuspearsbio-6)
DuBois was known as the "most powerful person in the music industry" by _Business Nashville_ in 1996, "Record Executive of the Year" in 1992 by _Pollstar_, and was included in _Entertainment Weekly_'s list of the "101 Most Powerful People in Entertainment" in 1994 and 1995. He is a member of Oklahoma State University's Hall of Fame (1996) and was the school's Accounting Alumnus of the year (1992).

## Early career in accounting
[edit]
He was born in Southwest City, Missouri. He started playing guitar in rock bands as a youth in nearby Grove, Oklahoma.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-lecture-7) He is a citizen of the Cherokee Nation.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-Okla_HOF-4) In his senior year of high school, a camp roommate wrote a song; DuBois was interested in song lyrics.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-lecture-7) He attended Oklahoma State University and studied accounting, winning three scholarships: an Arthur Andersen Scholarship, an Atlantic Richfield Scholarship and an Oklahoma State Regents Scholarship.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-osuspearsbio-6) He received a [bachelor's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor's_degree "Bachelor's degree") in accounting in 1971 and a [master's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master's_degree "Master's degree") in 1972, and he became a Certified Public Accountant (CPA).
He worked for the Arthur Andersen firm for about a year, then took a job in Dallas as a financial analyst for the Texas Federal Reserve Bank.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-aacsbhonor-8) During his time in Texas, he became interested in country music and pursued songwriting in his spare time. While attending an accounting convention in Dallas, he met up with his former professors, who convinced him to return to Oklahoma State to enter the PhD program at OSU's Spears School of Business. While in the PhD program, he said, "I'm a true left-brain, right-brain conflict, but it has served me very well".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-hutsongrandlake-9)

## Reorienting career to music
[edit]
In 1975, he met Scott Hendricks, another Oklahoma State student. Dubois and Hendricks, along with DuBois's younger brother (also a musician), headed to Nashville.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-lecture-7)
In 1979, he was given his first job as a publishing company staff songwriter by Bob Montgomery for $75 a week. From 1979 to 1985, DuBois worked as both a publishing company staff writer and as an accounting professor. Throughout that period, DuBois composed over 20 country singles. In 1980, he got a job teaching at Owen Graduate School of Management and he had three hit songs on the country charts: "Midnight Hauler" (Razzy Bailey); "Love in the First Degree" (Alabama);[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-reedgold-10) and "She Got the Goldmine (I Got the Shaft)" (Jerry Reed).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-11) DuBois opened the Nashville branch of Los Angeles-based artist management firm Fitzgerald-Hartley in 1986. Country artist Vince Gill became a Fitzgerald-Hartley client. DuBois and Gill collaborated on some songwriting projects, including the song "When I Call Your Name".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-12)
In 1989, Clive Davis, founder of Arista Records, appointed DuBois to open the Nashville division of the label. Arista Nashville sold 80 million albums in its first eleven years of business, breaking acts like Alan Jackson, Brooks & Dunn, Pam Tillis, Diamond Rio and Brad Paisley. DuBois later joined producer Tony Brown to operate Universal South Records.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-UniversalSouth-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-Tim_DuBois_Biography-14)

## Reorienting career to music
In 1991, DuBois married Pamela Smith from Dallas, Texas, a friend he had known for fifteen years. Their daughter, Jamie Grace DuBois, was born in 1994.
In 2007, DuBois returned to the faculty of Vanderbilt's Owen Graduate School of Management, where he is developing courses related to the music business. He has also joined forces with Marc Dottore to form Dottore-DuBois Artist Management.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-15) DuBois resides in Nashville, Tennessee. ASCAP announced in February 2010 that they would relocate their Nashville location to a DuBois-led regional office. DuBois holds the positions of Vice President and Managing Executive.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-ASCAP-16) After restructuring ASCAP, DuBois was asked to join London Broadcast Company in January 2012. He started a joint venture called AMP (Artists, Managers, Partners).
DuBois serves on the boards of the Country Music Association, the Academy of Country Music, the Americana Music Association, and SunTrust Bank, and as chairman of the Nashville Convention and Visitors Bureau. He is a past board member of Leadership Music,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_DuBois#cite_note-17)Country Music Foundation, National Academy of Recording Arts & Sciences, Nashville Songwriters Foundation, and Nashville Songwriters Association International.

**Visitation will be from Noon-7:00 p.m. on Sunday, November 16, 2025, at North Miami High School. We ask that you use the West “Football” doors to enter the school.**
Timothy E. DuBois, 79, of Peru, Indiana, passed away on November 9, 2025, surrounded by his loving family.
Born on November 18, 1945, to Thomas and Ida (Wagoner) DuBois, Tim grew up around the small town of Macy, Indiana. He was a 1963 graduate of North Miami High School and continued his education at McMurray College in Abilene, Texas, before completing his degree at Manchester University, where he played football and served as co-captain. Tim later earned his master’s degree in education from St. Francis College in Fort Wayne, Indiana.
In 1968, Tim began his long and influential teaching career at North Miami High School, where he taught physical education, health, and German. Over his 44 years at North Miami, Tim coached varsity football, wrestling, softball, track & field, and boys basketball. He also served as Athletic Director for 10 years.
A lifelong coach and mentor, Tim dedicated 51 years to coaching football and was co-founder of the Indiana Wishbone Association (IWA) Camp, where he helped shape generations of athletes and coaches. He was inducted into the Indiana Football Hall of Fame in 2022 and proudly served as assistant coach of the 1993 Class 1A State Championship team. In recognition of his enduring impact, North Miami High School named its football field “Tim DuBois Field” in 2019.
Outside of coaching, Tim was a talented fastpitch softball player and served as catcher for numerous teams, including Denver Tavern, Club 14, Peru Merchants, East End Fuel, Dietzen’s Bakery, Maple McCarty, and the Circus City Clowns.
Since the school’s opening in 1961, Tim’s life and legacy have been deeply intertwined with North Miami High School. Except for his years away at college, he remained an active and devoted part of the North Miami community throughout his life.

Tim is survived by his beloved wife, Linda DuBois; daughter Ann (Sissy) Martin and husband Brian Martin of Peru, Indiana; son James (Jimmy) DuBois of Kokomo, Indiana; granddaughter Abigail (Abby) Martin of Peru, Indiana; two step-granddaughters, Rebecca Martin (Andrew) and Sara (Mark) Greene; and four step-great-grandchildren. He is also survived by his mother-in-law Rosalie Weideman; brothers Robert (Bob) and Kay DuBois of Warsaw, Indiana, Donnie and Chris DuBois of Magnolia,Texas, and Dan (Mary) DuBois of Boulder, Colorado; sisters-in-law Sharon DuBois of Eugene, Oregon, Faithel DuBois of Pawleys Island, South Carolina, Patricia (Pat) Gahs and husband Denny Gahs of Clearwater, Florida, and Kathy Kline of Peru, Indiana; and niece Erica Kline of Peru, Indiana, along with several other nieces and nephews.
He was preceded in death by his parents, Thomas and Ida DuBois; brothers Phil DuBois and Dave DuBois; sister Diane (DuBois) Burge; and brother-in-law Sam Baker.
Tim will be remembered for his lifelong dedication to teaching, coaching, and community—his passion for sports, his love for his students and players, and his unwavering commitment to North Miami High School. Above all, he cherished his family, whose love and support meant the world to him. Tim was proud of the many roles he played in life — coach, athletic director, teacher — but nothing filled his heart more than being known as Pa. His legacy will continue to inspire all those whose lives he touched.
In lieu of flowers, contributions may be made through the funeral home to Relay for Life. McClain Funeral Home, PO Box 248, Denver, Indiana 46926. Envelopes will be available at the visitation
McClain Funeral Home, Denver, Indiana, has been entrusted with arrangements. Condolences may be sent online at www.mcclainfh.com.

Timothy F. Dubois, age 64, a cherished soul known for his friendly demeanor and kind heart, passed away unexpectedly at his home of 30 years in Hull, MA, on October 5, 2024. Born in Lawrence, MA, and raised in the neighboring town of Andover, Timothy's life was a testament to the love and strong bonds he shared with his family and friends.
Timothy was the beloved husband of Susan H. Dubois (Droney), with whom he shared a life filled with love and companionship. He was born to the late Gerard and Eileen Dubois, who instilled in him the values of family and hard work. As a caring brother, he leaves behind Stephen Dubois and his wife Abbie of Louisiana, Kathy Doerr and her husband Ed of Methuen, Christopher Dubois of New Hampshire, and Mark Dubois also of New Hampshire. His nieces and nephews will remember him fondly for his warmth and playful spirit. Tim was proud to be a part of the Dubois / McIntyre clan of over 70 cousins.
An alumnus of Andover High School, Tim went on to work initially at Raytheon, and then in building maintenance at Saks 5th Ave, Episcopal Divinity School and finally a member of Local 32BJ at Leslie College. His colleagues knew him as someone always ready to lend a helping hand or share a friendly conversation.
Outside of work, Tim's interests were simple yet deeply cherished. He had a passion for playing the lottery and was considered quite lucky. Tim loved music, cars, Boston sports and various vacation destinations.
Above all, Tim found the greatest pleasure in the comforts of home. He especially enjoyed relaxing with a glass of wine, from his perch over Nantasket Beach, shared in the company of his loved ones. His presence at home was a source of stability and warmth, which extended to sharing in the care of his mother-in-law, Ruth, when called upon.
Tim's friendly nature extended beyond his immediate circle. He had the rare ability to make anyone feel at home, greeting friends and strangers alike. Always with jokes and a smile, his spirit remains with all who knew him.

As we say farewell to Timothy F. Dubois, we celebrate a life lived with generosity and love. His story is not only about the moments he shared but also about the countless lives he touched with his gentle presence. Though he has left us too soon, the impact of his life's journey will resonate for years to come, a testament to a life well-lived and a man dearly loved.
Visiting hours at the Dockray & Thomas Funeral Home 455 Washington St. Canton Sunday 3:00 to 6:00. Funeral Mass at St. Oscar Romero Church, Canton Monday morning at 10:00. Burial Canton Corner Cemetery.
To send flowers to the family or plant a tree in memory of Timothy F. Dubois, please visit our floral store.

Tim DuBois, born November 18, 1945, in Macy, Indiana, devoted much of his life to the North Miami community, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of leadership, dedication, and service to high school athletics. A proud graduate of North Miami High School in the Class of 1963, DuBois held a special place in the school's history as its second football captain. His connection to North Miami would become a lifelong commitment, spanning generations of student-athletes and countless seasons on the sidelines.
After attending McMurry College, where he earned his bachelor's degree, and Manchester College, where he earned his master's degree, DuBois returned to North Miami High School when the school opened in 1965. With the exception of his time in college, he remained involved in the North Miami community throughout his life, continuing to serve the school and its athletic programs even into his later years. His dedication extended well beyond the football field, as he served North Miami as Athletic Director, Head Football Coach, Head Wrestling Coach, and Head Softball Coach.

Over the course of an extraordinary 52 seasons coaching football, DuBois became an integral part of North Miami football history. He was involved in every football championship in the school's history, contributing to a tradition of success that left a lasting mark on the program. Among his many accomplishments was his role as offensive line coach for the 1993 Class 1A State Championship team, a remarkable squad that featured four 1,000-yard rushers. His coaching experience also extended beyond North Miami, as he served as an assistant coach for the North All-Star team in 1994.
The impact of DuBois's contributions to North Miami is permanently recognized through the naming of the school's football field in his honor: Tim DuBois Field. It is a fitting tribute to a man whose life was so closely connected to the school, its athletic programs, and the young people who represented it. His influence reached far beyond wins and championships, reflecting a lifetime of commitment to the community he called home.
Away from the field, Tim shared his life with his wife, Linda. Together, they raised two children, Ann Marie (DuBois) Martin and Jimmy DuBois, and welcomed one granddaughter, Abby Martin. His family remained an important part of the life he built alongside his many years of service to North Miami.
On September 9, 2022, at North Miami High School, DuBois was inducted into the Indiana Football Hall of Fame, representing IFCA Region 5 and North Miami High School as a coach. The recognition celebrated a career defined by 52 seasons of coaching, extraordinary loyalty to one school, and a lasting contribution to Indiana high school football.
Tim DuBois passed away in 2025, but his legacy remains firmly rooted at North Miami. From his days as a student and football captain to his decades as a coach, athletic director, and mentor, his story is woven into the history of the school. With a football field bearing his name and generations of North Miami athletes shaped by his dedication, Tim DuBois will forever be remembered as an important part of North Miami football.

Timothy E. DuBois, 79, of Peru, Indiana, passed away on November 9, 2025, surrounded by his loving family.
Born on November 18, 1945, to Thomas and Ida (Wagoner) DuBois, Tim grew up around the small town of Macy, Indiana. He was a 1963 graduate of North Miami High School and continued his education at McMurray College in Abilene, Texas, before completing his degree at Manchester University, where he played football and served as co-captain. Tim later earned his master’s degree in education from St. Francis College in Fort Wayne, Indiana.
In 1968, Tim began his long and influential teaching career at North Miami High School, where he taught physical education, health, and German. Over his 44 years at North Miami, Tim coached varsity football, wrestling, softball, track & field, and boys basketball. He also served as Athletic Director for 10 years.
A lifelong coach and mentor, Tim dedicated 51 years to coaching football and was co-founder of the Indiana Wishbone Association (IWA) Camp, where he helped shape generations of athletes and coaches. He was inducted into the Indiana Football Hall of Fame in 2022 and proudly served as assistant coach of the 1993 Class 1A State Championship team. In recognition of his enduring impact, North Miami High School named its football field “Tim DuBois Field” in 2019.
Outside of coaching, Tim was a talented fastpitch softball player and served as catcher for numerous teams, including Denver Tavern, Club 14, Peru Merchants, East End Fuel, Dietzen’s Bakery, Maple McCarty, and the Circus City Clowns.
Since the school’s opening in 1961, Tim’s life and legacy have been deeply intertwined with North Miami High School. Except for his years away at college, he remained an active and devoted part of the North Miami community throughout his life.

A proud graduate of North Miami High School in the Class of 1963, DuBois held a special place in the school's history as its second football captain. His connection to North Miami would become a lifelong commitment, spanning generations of student-athletes and countless seasons on the sidelines.

Timothy E. DuBois, 79, of Peru, Indiana, passed away on November 9, 2025, surrounded by his loving family.

Tim later earned his master’s degree in education from St. Francis College in Fort Wayne, Indiana.
In 1968, Tim began his long and influential teaching career at North Miami High School, where he taught physical education, health, and German. Over his 44 years at North Miami, Tim coached varsity football, wrestling, softball, track & field, and boys basketball. He also served as Athletic Director for 10 years.
A lifelong coach and mentor, Tim dedicated 51 years to coaching football and was co-founder of the Indiana Wishbone Association (IWA) Camp, where he helped shape generations of athletes and coaches. He was inducted into the Indiana Football Hall of Fame in 2022 and proudly served as assistant coach of the 1993 Class 1A State Championship team. In recognition of his enduring impact, North Miami High School named its football field “Tim DuBois Field” in 2019.
Outside of coaching, Tim was a talented fastpitch softball player and served as catcher for numerous teams, including Denver Tavern, Club 14, Peru Merchants, East End Fuel, Dietzen’s Bakery, Maple McCarty, and the Circus City Clowns.
